artifact_policy: The source package includes two complete synthetic runs, arxiv and Peptides-func, with checkpoints, predictions, prepared fixtures, stage seals and checksums. They demonstrate software workflows; they are not official benchmark observations. All seven dataset adapters and 21 profiles remain available. Official datasets and ordinary user runs stay outside the source tree.

scope_notes: Nine core policy families and the eight-stage lifecycle are available on all seven datasets.
Each task uses its declared loss, prediction axis and official metric.
Independent graph episodes reset predictor/controller/anchor state; graph-level predictions pool within one graph.
Roman-empire supports all ten official masks and a separate split-summary campaign.
Synthetic checks establish software behavior, not benchmark performance.

The budget-matched arms E3-E6 (including the budget-aware rule q_B) and the pinned-upstream driver of the retrained external baselines are implemented in cm_experiments/ and run outside the eight-stage lifecycle; their outputs enter as record sets through scripts/export_records.py. The upstream baseline code and its task adapters are pinned by commit in each study plan, not bundled.
Manuscript agreement requires explicit bindings to the corresponding result-producing artifacts.
The manuscript's registered constants and reported results are kept as transcriptions in paper/ and verified against the executable registry and the full profiles by scripts/check_paper_constants.py.
The implementation choices the manuscript leaves open are recorded in paper/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md.
